paper.title: Questioning the Coverage-Length Metric in Conformal Prediction: When Shorter Intervals Are Not Better

claims.paper_claim: The Prejudicial Trick can shorten intervals while retaining marginal coverage.
claims.scope: 100 finite source-protocol rows across five seeds, four alpha values, and five p values; 16/16 nontrivial conditions shorter.

claims.paper_claim: Table 1 synthetic values and source protocol are reproduced.
claims.scope: Current author snapshot matches the clean-room output; bias-10 matches historical CSV to 7.1e-15, while the paper's p=0.96 PT value differs.

claims.paper_claim: The real-world regression comparison shows the PT length effect.
claims.scope: Seven obtainable UCI datasets ran, including three paper datasets; unavailable datasets and checkpoints are not substituted.

claims.paper_claim: PT interval instability is exposed by repeated runs and p=1 is a deterministic control.
claims.scope: 80 positive-stability p<1 rows and 20 deterministic p=1 controls; independent false-positive and false-negative counts are zero.

claims.paper_claim: Localized conformal prediction contains the PT extreme case.
claims.scope: 15 conditions, 1,500,000 retrainings, zero samplewise interval mismatches, and a passing p=1 control.

claims.paper_claim: A trained local-scale estimator demonstrates the broader instability mechanism.
claims.scope: Three seeds and 20 retrains per seed; mean localized IS 0.05465, VCP IS 0, and mean localized coverage 0.90625.

limitations: Finite checks do not prove the paper's theorem or exchangeability assumptions.
The full Section 4/5 dataset, classification, ablation, and checkpoint suite is not reproduced.
The Table 1 p=0.96 discrepancy and bias-20 source drift are retained as audit results.
No official score or author endorsement is claimed.
